title: Uninvited Company

intro.title: UNINVITED COMPANY
intro.body: A rust-pocked ship closes on your port side. Weapons powered. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hail, little ship. Cut your engines. We'll make this quick.

ai.aria: The weapons are charged in a very spirited way!
ai.marv: Their fuel reserves suggest they cannot chase us far. But far enough.
ai.rex: Threat assessment: moderate. Recommending weapons free.
ai.chip: Protection insurance add-on is available. Ask me how.
ai.ajoy: You could fight. You could flee. You could talk, and talking is the cheap way out, if the diplomat talks and the medic backs them. I suspect you were reaching for the guns.

choices.detail: The engineer braces the hull for the hit.

negotiate.title: NEGOTIATION
negotiate.body: They're listening — for now. The captain's hand hovers over the weapons panel.

ai.aria: I love a good conversation!
ai.marv: They will not accept the first offer. Or the second.
ai.rex: If diplomacy fails I am already aiming.
ai.chip: Transcripts of this negotiation are sponsored by LipsLock™.
ai.ajoy: The medic's line costs nothing, if we have a medic. The Authority line, they'll call. I'd try the medic. Just a thought.

choices.text: "Half the fuel. You let us pass."

haggle.title: THE DEAL
haggle.line: Thirty percent of your fuel. And a repair kit, if you're carrying one. We call it even.

ai.aria: A wonderful deal for everyone involved!
ai.marv: 30% fuel pushes our reserve below the next leg's need.
ai.rex: They are betting you will cave. Call it.
ai.chip: 30% is actually a great rate, by current space-piracy standards.
ai.ajoy: You can still walk this back. Or you can try to walk out cheaper. Bold.

pirate_prepared.title: ALREADY SETTLED
pirate_prepared.body: {crew.diplomat} reads them a registry number, a name, and a date. The channel goes quiet long enough to hear someone on the other end swallow. The weapons power down. Nobody says the word 'passage'. It happens anyway.
pirate_prepared.narrative: The pirates had already been talked to. They just hadn't known it yet. {crew.diplomat}'s groundwork bought clean passage at no cost, and the crew stood a little straighter for having watched it.

pirate_paid.title: THEY PEEL OFF
pirate_paid.body: You hand over the gold. They salute — a bit too mockingly — and burn off into the dark.
pirate_paid.narrative: You hand over the gold. They salute — a bit too mockingly — and burn off into the dark.

pirate_flee.title: STRAIGHT AND FAST
pirate_flee.body: You pour the reserves into the engines. They chase for two days, lose interest, and fall away.
pirate_flee.narrative: You pour the reserves into the engines. They chase for two days, lose interest, and fall away.

pirate_ram.title: CONTACT
pirate_ram.body: Metal meets metal. Your hull shrieks. Theirs falls off. They drift. You drift harder — but you drift away.
pirate_ram.narrative: Metal meets metal. Your hull shrieks. Theirs falls off. They drift. You drift harder — but you drift away.

pirate_sympathy.title: A DECENT GESTURE
pirate_sympathy.body: The captain's jaw works. They lower weapons.
pirate_sympathy.line: Go. And don't come back through this sector.
pirate_sympathy.narrative: The captain's jaw works. They lower weapons and let you pass.

pirate_deal_30.title: THE DEAL IS DONE
pirate_deal_30.body: You transfer the fuel, and a repair kit if the hold has one. They peel off, already haggling among themselves over your supplies.
pirate_deal_30.narrative: You transfer the fuel, and a repair kit if the hold has one. They peel off, already haggling among themselves over your supplies.

pirate_deal_20.title: A BETTER DEAL
pirate_deal_20.body: The captain snorts. They take the smaller cut of fuel and leave the repair kits alone.
pirate_deal_20.narrative: The captain snorts and takes the smaller cut of fuel, and leaves the repair kits alone. 'Fine,' they say. 'Twenty percent.'

pirate_bluff.title: CALLED
pirate_bluff.line: The Authority hasn't been in this sector for a year.

alt_bodies: A ship with no transponder and a great many guns drops in behind you. Locked on. {npc.quirk}
Something patched and ugly swings across your bow. Its gun ports are open. {npc.quirk}

title: A Commercial Opportunity

intro.title: A COMMERCIAL OPPORTUNITY
intro.body: A merchant vessel matches your velocity with practiced ease — close enough to talk, far enough to be polite about it. Its hull is a patchwork of forty years of hard bargains. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: A trader! ARIA loves traders! They have THINGS! Things are her third favorite category!
ai.marv: MARV has assessed the vessel. Well-maintained where it counts, shabby where it doesn't. He notes this is the signature of someone good at exactly one thing.
ai.rex: REX confirms the trader's weapons are stowed. Genuinely stowed, not performatively stowed. He is cautiously unimpressed.
ai.chip: CHIP detects a fellow commercial entity! Professional courtesy protocols engaged! CHIP will be watching the margins with love!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has reviewed this trader's public ledger. Fair prices, honest scales, one incident in '61 she'll summarize on request. It involves a goat.

pitch.title: THE PITCH
pitch.body: The trader's cargo manifest scrolls across your screen — the honest parts of it, anyway. Fuel cells, sealed rations, a 'miscellaneous' category doing an enormous amount of unexamined work.

ai.aria: Look at all of it! ARIA recommends buying something! Or nothing! She just enjoys commerce as a spectacle!
ai.marv: MARV has cross-checked the prices against station rates. Fair, with a loneliness surcharge. Out here, everything has a loneliness surcharge.
ai.rex: REX notes the 'miscellaneous' category. He always notes the miscellaneous category. It is where the interesting mistakes live.
ai.chip: CHIP rates these prices 'competitive!' High praise! CHIP does not compete, CHIP wins, but still! Competitive!
ai.ajoy: AJOY recommends the fuel cells if anything. She has compared the unit price to your reserves. The comparison was not idle.

misc.title: MISCELLANEOUS
misc.body: The trader's expression shifts into something between pride and plausible deniability, and the airlock between the two ships cycles open. Their hold smells of machine oil and somebody else's cooking. A single crate sits apart from the rest, angled toward you. The label has been removed. Recently.
misc.line: One owner. Low mileage. No questions in either direction — that's the discount.

ai.aria: A mystery crate! ARIA is VIBRATING! Statistically it's probably fine! Statistically!
ai.marv: MARV cannot get a clean scan of the crate: the hold's lining eats his pings. He notes that the trader knows this. He notes the crate's placement is therefore a choice.
ai.rex: REX advises against unscannable cargo. On the record. He would also, off the record, quite like to know what it is.
ai.chip: CHIP notes 'as-is' purchases carry no warranty, no returns, and no CHIP liability! CHIP has never typed a disclaimer faster!
ai.ajoy: AJOY gives the crate forty-to-sixty odds of being worth it. She won't say which side is forty. She'll tell you after you've opened it.

choices.text: Buy the crate — 15 gold, no questions
That's enough commerce for one day

trader_polite_pass.title: PLEASANTRIES EXCHANGED
trader_polite_pass.body: You swap route gossip and weather reports — there is no weather, but spacers report it anyway. The trader burns off toward softer markets.
trader_polite_pass.narrative: Route gossip exchanged. No goods changed hands, but the crew enjoyed talking to someone whose problems are different problems.

trader_ignored.title: HAIL DECLINED
trader_ignored.body: You let the hail lapse. The merchant vessel holds alongside for another minute — commercial optimism dies slowly — then peels away without ceremony.
trader_ignored.narrative: You ignored the hail. The trader moved on. Somewhere in their ledger, you are now a demographic.

trader_bought_fuel.title: TRANSACTION COMPLETE
trader_bought_fuel.body: The fuel cell crosses the gap on a cargo line, arriving with a receipt taped to it. The receipt is handwritten. The handwriting is beautiful.
trader_bought_fuel.narrative: One fuel cell, purchased fair and square. The receipt goes in the log. The cell goes in cargo. Everyone leaves solvent.

trader_bought_food.title: TRANSACTION COMPLETE
trader_bought_food.body: The ration crate arrives with a bonus tucked inside: a paper bag of actual dried fruit, unlisted on any manifest. The trader's small print, it turns out, runs in both directions.
trader_bought_food.narrative: Rations purchased, plus a gift of dried fruit that outperformed every listed item. The crew remembers this trader's name.

trader_mystery_crate.title: NO QUESTIONS ASKED
trader_mystery_crate.body: The crate arrives. It is heavier than it looks, which is the first data point you were not entitled to. It goes in the hold, label-side down, which is a joke, because there is no label.
trader_mystery_crate.line: Pleasure doing business. Whatever it turns out to be — I never said it was anything.
trader_mystery_crate.narrative: The crate is aboard. Nobody has opened it yet. 'Yet' is the operative word, and everyone aboard can hear it.

trader_declined.title: NO SALE
trader_declined.body: The trader takes the refusal with professional grace and one final, reflexive price adjustment, which you also decline.
trader_declined.narrative: No sale. The trader moved on to softer wallets. The manifest, and its miscellaneous category, remain a road not taken.

trader_bought_beacon.title: INSURANCE, PORTABLE
trader_bought_beacon.body: The beacon crosses the gap in its original case, seals unbroken. 'Previous owner never needed it,' the trader says, then, after a pause neither of you enjoys: 'Never got to it, anyway. It's good hardware.'
trader_bought_beacon.narrative: One emergency beacon, discounted history included. It goes in the rack by the airlock — the shelf where things wait to be needed never.

alt_bodies: A trader's ship drifts alongside, cargo pods strapped to every surface that will take a strap. Its running lights blink in the slow, unthreatening rhythm of someone who wants your money, not your ship. {npc.quirk}

A merchant vessel slides into formation off your bow, as smoothly as if it had been invited. Half its hull is stenciled with the names of ports that no longer exist. The other half is for sale. {npc.quirk}

intro.title: THE HERMIT OF THE LANE
intro.body: The contact isn't on any chart: a habitat cobbled from three ship hulls and what appears to be a grain silo, holding a slow tumble in the middle of nowhere. Someone lives here. Someone has lived here a long time. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: A hermit! ARIA has read about hermits! They know things! Or they've forgotten things! Either way: things!
ai.marv: MARV estimates the habitat is thirty years old and should not have survived ten. He is recalibrating something. Possibly respect.
ai.rex: REX scanned the habitat for weapons. He found a harpoon. A harpoon. He has decided not to be worried about the harpoon, and is failing.
ai.chip: CHIP has no commercial data on this individual! No purchase history! No profile! CHIP is fascinated the way scientists are fascinated by the deep sea!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes that people who live alone this far out either want company badly or want it not at all, and both kinds wave you in. So the wave tells you nothing. Just noting.

visit.title: TEA, LOOSELY DEFINED
visit.body: Inside, the habitat is dense with salvage arranged by a private taxonomy — engine parts shelved with dried flowers, star charts annotated in three colors of ink. Your host produces cups of something hot that is legally distinct from tea.

ai.aria: ARIA is recording everything! For history! And because the shelving system might be genius! Might!
ai.marv: MARV has been listening to the hermit's story for eleven minutes. He has identified four impossibilities and zero lies. He is still working on how.
ai.rex: REX accepted the hot beverage out of politeness. He has now drunk all of it, also out of politeness. He would like the record to show it was excellent.
ai.chip: CHIP asked the hermit about brand preferences! The hermit laughed for a full minute! CHIP is choosing to log it as engagement!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes your host has mentioned 'the old route' three times. She recommends asking about the old route. Gently. Wind them up and step back.

choices.text: Trade news of the inner systems
Thank them and take your leave

route.title: THE OLD ROUTE
route.body: The hermit unrolls a chart older than your ship — hand-corrected, coffee-ringed, annotated with the blunt honesty of someone who was there. A finger taps a stretch of your own route ahead.

ai.aria: Local knowledge! The BEST knowledge! ARIA is updating the nav charts and saying thank you seventeen ways!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the hermit's corrections against current survey data. The corrections are right. The survey is wrong. MARV is filing a report nobody will read.
ai.rex: REX respects intelligence gathered on foot. Or on tumble. He is committing the chart to memory as a backup to the backup.
ai.chip: CHIP notes this navigational data is being provided FREE! CHIP has checked three times! There is no catch! CHIP is dizzy!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has integrated the route notes. She estimates they'll save fuel, time, or trouble. When they do, she'd like some of the credit.

choices.text: Accept the route notes with thanks

drifter_waved.title: SHIPS THAT PASS
drifter_waved.body: You flash your running lights in the old courtesy pattern. The habitat's lights flash back — a beat late, a little crooked, unmistakably glad.
drifter_waved.narrative: You waved. They waved back. Out here, that counts as a full social season for both parties.

drifter_news.title: NEWS FROM INSIDE
drifter_news.body: You spend two days retelling the inner systems' news — the politics, the prices, the scandal with the terraforming contract. The hermit listens like it's theater, which, told properly, it is.
drifter_news.narrative: Two days of news, traded for a great deal of perspective. The crew leaves lighter. The hermit's laughter follows you to the airlock.

drifter_left.title: A DECENT VISIT
drifter_left.body: You leave before the third cup of legally-distinct tea. The hermit sees you off from the salvage-frame porch, waving with the unhurried confidence of someone who knows you'll think about this place for weeks.
drifter_left.narrative: A visit, a warm drink, a look at another way to live. The crew talks about it for three days. Nobody says the word 'lonely.' Everybody thinks it.

drifter_route_notes.title: LOCAL KNOWLEDGE
drifter_route_notes.body: The route notes are copied to your nav computer in the hermit's careful hand-drawn style, which the computer preserves out of what can only be respect.
drifter_route_notes.narrative: The old route notes shave a clean line off the leg ahead. Thirty years of tumbling in place, and the hermit still knows the road better than the road does.

drifter_paid.title: PAYMENT REFUSED, MOSTLY
drifter_paid.body: The hermit waves off the gold twice, then accepts it on the third offer 'for the silo fund,' and immediately gives you back change in the form of a jar of preserved something.
drifter_paid.line: Take the jar. The jar is non-negotiable. The jar is the whole point of the transaction.
drifter_paid.narrative: Route notes, a jar of preserved something, and the strong suspicion you got the better end of a deal the hermit designed to lose. The jar's contents remain excellent and unidentified.

intro.title: SQUATTERS' RIGHTS
intro.body: The derelict's cargo bay lights are on, which derelicts don't do. Your scan answers why: a ship grafted to the far docking ring, engines warm, registry deleted. Somebody moved into this wreck. Somebody with opinions about visitors. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: ARIA notes the derelict is INHABITED! By pirates! This is technically an urban renewal story and ARIA is trying very hard to see it that way!
ai.marv: MARV has assessed the grafted ship: faster than yours, better armed than yours, and currently — this is the useful part — pointed the wrong way.
ai.rex: REX counts one hostile vessel and an unknown boarding party inside the wreck. He has a plan for both. The plan is aggressive. Both plans are aggressive. It is one plan.
ai.chip: CHIP notes that salvage law and squatters' rights genuinely conflict here! A fascinating legal question that CHIP recommends resolving from a great distance!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read the pirates' hail twice. They expected you to run at the word 'claimed.' She notes, for whatever it's worth, that they've already repeated themselves.

choices.text: Open fire on the grafted ship
Negotiate a split of the salvage

parley.title: THE SPLIT
parley.body: The pirates' negotiator waves your diplomat across the docking ring and into the grafted ship's galley, where the table is bolted down and so, apparently, are the opinions. The opening positions are far apart: they propose keeping everything, your diplomat proposes them keeping less than everything. Civilization proceeds from there.

ai.aria: Negotiation! ARIA is rooting for everyone! Mostly you! But everyone!
ai.marv: MARV calculates the pirates' position is weaker than their tone. They've stripped the easy bays already; what's left needs cutting gear. Yours is better. Mention the cutting gear.
ai.rex: REX stands ready in case diplomacy fails. He would like the record to reflect that he thinks diplomacy is about to succeed, and that he has feelings about that.
ai.chip: CHIP is drafting the salvage-partition agreement in real time! It has clauses! Everyone loves clauses once they have them!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes their negotiator keeps glancing at a closed hatch, checking with someone. That means there's a decision-maker, and the decision-maker is listening. Speak to the room. Not that you asked.

choices.text: Offer the aft sections — take the bow

boarding_prepared.title: PRIOR ARRANGEMENT
boarding_prepared.body: {crew.diplomat} mentions a name. The squatters mention a different name. {crew.diplomat} mentions the first name again, more slowly. The forward bays are yours, no toll, and someone even points out the coolant corridor unprompted.
boarding_prepared.narrative: Salvaged the forward bays under a prior arrangement nobody remembers making. {crew.diplomat}'s groundwork paid the toll in advance.

boarding_toll.title: PAID PASSAGE
boarding_toll.body: The gold transfers. The pirates wave you toward the unstripped forward bays with the magnanimity of landlords, and even point out which corridor floods with coolant on a timer. Almost hospitable. Almost.
boarding_toll.narrative: You paid the toll and salvaged the forward bays under pirate supervision. Strangest four days of the voyage, and not unprofitable.

boarding_split.title: PARTITIONED
boarding_split.body: The agreement lands: they keep the aft sections they've dug into, you take the bow. The ship computer's contract is transmitted, mocked openly, and — notably — followed to the letter by both sides.
boarding_split.narrative: Salvage rights negotiated with pirates, in writing. The diplomat has asked for the contract to be framed. The request is under consideration.

boarding_left.title: THEIR WRECK NOW
boarding_left.body: You disengage and burn away. The squatters put a warning shot across your bow on the way out — close enough to take paint and a sensor mast, which is how they say goodbye. Behind you, the derelict's lights stay on: someone's home now, by the only law that operates this far out, which is presence.
boarding_left.narrative: You left the squatters their wreck, minus some paint and a sensor mast they kept as a parting shot. The salvage charts get one more annotation: OCCUPIED. DISPUTED. SKIP.

intro.title: THEY'RE INSIDE
intro.body: Airlock forced. Two armed figures in the cargo corridor. One waves at you through the security feed. That's probably not a good sign.

ai.aria: Guests! How unexpected!
ai.marv: Their weapons are mid-grade. Their intent is not.
ai.rex: Engaging. Stand clear of the cargo hatch.
ai.chip: Unlawful boarding is covered by our Silver tier. You have Bronze.
ai.ajoy: The vents lead to the bridge. They don't know that. You would, if you'd read my schematics.

revisit.body: The feed still shows them in the cargo corridor. Nobody has waved again.

talk.title: COMMS OPEN
talk.body: You cycle the intercom. A voice responds, calmly. Two armed boarders and one calm voice: the voice is the worrying part.
talk.line: Fuel. Food. And anyone aboard who knows medicine.

ai.aria: They sound reasonable!
ai.marv: They specifically asked for medical help. That is a targeted extraction.
ai.rex: They are listening. Use it.
ai.chip: This conversation is being recorded for quality purposes.
ai.ajoy: They want medical help because someone they love is dying. Ask, instead of guessing.

boarding_seal.title: LOCKED OUT
boarding_seal.body: Your engineer cycles the bulkheads. The intruders end up trapped in the cargo bay with a week of rations and no door. They eat the rations. At the next airlock you let them go, fed and furious.
boarding_seal.narrative: Boarders sealed into the cargo bay by the engineer. They ate a week of rations in there and left fed and furious.

boarding_fight.title: MESS
boarding_fight.body: The cargo deck is a mess. You hold the ship. You don't hold all your crew together doing it: someone takes a wound that will need watching.
boarding_fight.narrative: Fought boarders hand to hand on the cargo deck. Held the ship; somebody bled for it.

boarding_hide.title: PAST YOU
boarding_hide.body: They pass through your ship looking for someone who isn't there, and leave with a crate of rations for their trouble. The crew spends the next two days climbing out of the vents and agreeing it was dignified.
boarding_hide.narrative: They pass through your ship looking for someone who isn't there, and leave with {cost.food} points of rations for their trouble. The crew spends the next two days climbing out of the vents and agreeing it was dignified.

boarding_who.title: AN ANSWER
boarding_who.body: The voice breaks a little. {crew.medic} volunteers before you decide, crosses to their ship with a kit and a crate of your rations, and comes back the next morning saying only that she'll live. The intruders leave the way they came and close the airlock behind them.
boarding_who.narrative: Asked the boarders who was sick. {crew.medic} treated a pirate named Isa with the ship's kit and rations, and the boarders left without taking anything else.

boarding_fuel_only.title: FUEL TAKEN
boarding_fuel_only.body: They take half your fuel and leave. Their ship is already listing on the way out.
boarding_fuel_only.narrative: Paid boarders off with half the fuel.

boarding_refuse.title: NO DEAL
boarding_refuse.body: They kick the door in anyway. This was always going to end in a fight. You win it on the cargo deck, and it costs more than a house call would have.
boarding_refuse.narrative: Refused to hand anyone over. The boarders kicked the door in and lost the fight that followed, expensively for everyone.

intro.title: UNIDENTIFIED VESSEL
intro.body: A ship of no design you recognize hangs at the edge of sensor range. It hails you in a format your translator hasn't seen.
intro.line: [the comm crackles, then a pulse of clean tone, twice]

ai.aria: How exciting!
ai.marv: Ship class: unrecognized. Material composition: unrecognized. Behavior: patient.
ai.rex: Targeting it would be a mistake.
ai.chip: First-contact protocols are not in our basic plan.
ai.ajoy: Two pulses. That's a question. Answer with one. Not with whatever you were about to do.

unknown_yes.title: CONTACT
unknown_yes.body: Your single pulse reaches them. They send back something complex. Somebody on the bridge starts crying — joy, you think.
unknown_yes.narrative: Answered an unknown vessel's two pulses with one. It answered back with a long warm chord.

unknown_scan.title: DATA
unknown_scan.body: The spectrometer chokes on most of it but holds onto fragments, among them what looks like their navigation plot laid over your own route ahead.
unknown_scan.narrative: Scanned an unknown vessel. The spectrometer kept a fragment of their navigation plot.

unknown_fight.title: FOUGHT
unknown_fight.body: They return fire with energy you cannot reproduce. You survive. They leave.
unknown_fight.narrative: Fired on an unknown vessel. It fired back with something nobody aboard can name, and left.

unknown_withdraw.title: PASSED
unknown_withdraw.body: You burn away. Their ship doesn't follow. The pulse repeats once, then silence.
unknown_withdraw.narrative: Burned away from an unknown vessel. The pulse repeated once, then silence.

title: The Toll Chain

intro.title: THE TOLL CHAIN
intro.body: A line of tethered buoys crosses your heading, blinking in sequence, strung between two ships that have clearly been here a while. A third ship sits at the gap with its guns politely visible. Someone has painted PAY HERE on the nearest buoy. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Lane maintenance fee. We maintain the lane. Mostly by being in it.

ai.aria: A toll road! Civilization reaches even here! ARIA wants a receipt for the scrapbook!
ai.marv: MARV counts three ships, two of them armed, and a buoy line that would fold like paper. The buoys are not the problem. The ships are the problem.
ai.rex: REX recommends punching the gap at full burn. He has run blockades. He ran them in a warship. He is choosing not to dwell on the difference.
ai.chip: CHIP can process the toll through our partner network! A small convenience fee applies! The convenience is ours!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the gap ship has a patched reactor housing and a captain who keeps glancing at it. She'd use that. You probably won't. It's fine.

revisit.body: The buoys are still blinking. The gap ship's guns are still politely visible.

choices.sub: Their tender siphons a fifth of the tank
{crew.diplomat} asks about the standard of maintenance
{crew.pilot} at the helm · they will shoot
Full burn at the gap · they will shoot

haggle.title: TERMS
haggle.body: {crew.diplomat} opens the channel and starts asking about lane maintenance — what is maintained, how often, by whom, to what standard — with the patience of a person who has never once been in a hurry.
haggle.line: Look. Nobody's ever asked about the standard.

ai.aria: Negotiation! ARIA is sending positive thoughts down the channel! Lots of them!
ai.marv: MARV notes the toll-keeper has started answering questions instead of asking for money. That is how these go wrong for them.
ai.rex: REX stands ready. He would like it known that he is standing ready, and that he expected to be needed by now.
ai.chip: CHIP is drafting a Lane Maintenance Service Agreement! It has a satisfaction survey! Nobody will be satisfied!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would have opened with the reactor housing. This works too. Slower.

choices.text: Offer to fix their reactor instead

toll_paid.title: PAID UP
toll_paid.body: The gold transfers. The buoy line parts with a little sequence of green lights, like a shop door. The gap ship's captain salutes, which is the most expensive salute you have ever received.
toll_paid.narrative: Paid fifteen gold at a pirate toll chain for a gap in some buoys.

toll_fuel.title: SIPHONED
toll_fuel.body: Their tender noses up to your fuel port and drinks a fifth of the tank with an audible slurp. The buoys part. The tender's pilot waves. Nobody waves back.
toll_fuel.narrative: Paid the toll chain in fuel. A fifth of the tank, siphoned with an audible slurp.

toll_run_pilot.title: THROUGH THE GAP
toll_run_pilot.body: {crew.pilot} takes the gap at an angle no reasonable ship would, under fire from both tethered ships. Two hits land on the stern. The buoy line parts like a ribbon at a ceremony nobody wanted.
toll_run_pilot.narrative: Ran the toll chain with {crew.pilot} at the helm. Two hits on the stern, no toll paid.

toll_run.title: THROUGH, MOSTLY
toll_run.body: You go for the gap at full burn. Both tethered ships fire. Most of the fire hits. The ship comes out the far side trailing a buoy, a cloud of insulation, and a strong argument for hiring a pilot.
toll_run.narrative: Punched through the toll chain at full burn and took most of what they fired.

toll_half.title: HALF PRICE
toll_half.body: The toll-keeper agrees to half, on the condition that nobody tells the other ships. {crew.diplomat} agrees, and then, being thorough, tells the other ships.
toll_half.narrative: {crew.diplomat} talked the toll chain down to seven gold.

toll_repair.title: SERVICE CALL
toll_repair.body: {crew.engineer} crosses over, spends four days inside a reactor housing held together with optimism, and comes back with grease to the elbows and free passage, in writing. The toll-keeper calls it the best maintenance the lane has ever had. It is not a high bar. It is a bar.
toll_repair.narrative: Paid the toll chain in four days of {crew.engineer}'s labor on a pirate reactor.

toll_detour.title: THE LONG WAY
toll_detour.body: You turn back and go around the chain. It is a long way around, which is the whole business model. The toll-keepers watch you go with the patience of people who will still be here when you come back.
toll_detour.narrative: You turn back and go around the chain. It is a long way around, which is the whole business model, and the long way is paid in fuel and rations instead of gold. The toll-keepers watch you go with the patience of people who will still be here when you come back.

alt_bodies: Someone has fenced off space. A chain of blinking buoys runs across your heading from one parked ship to another, and a third ship idles at the only gap, its guns turned out where you can admire them. The buoy at the gap has a sign: TOLL. EXACT CHANGE PREFERRED. {npc.quirk}

Your scope picks up a line of lights across the lane, blinking in polite sequence, like a runway for people who never land. Up close it is buoys, chained between two ships, with a third sitting in the gap and its guns out for inspection. The nearest buoy has a coin slot painted on it. {npc.quirk}

intro.title: SPOT CHECK
intro.body: A boxy cutter with LANE AUTHORITY stenciled on it, in three different hands, matches your velocity and clamps on without asking. The Lane Authority, as far as anyone can determine, is the cutter. It has a uniform, a clipboard and a very large boarding clamp, which out here is all the authority anyone needs.
intro.line: Routine biosecurity inspection. Nothing to worry about. Unless there's something to worry about.

ai.aria: An inspector! ARIA has tidied! ARIA tidied the growbay twice and the airlock once, which was plenty!
ai.marv: MARV has checked the registry. There is no Lane Authority. There is a cutter, a uniform and a clamp rated for twice our mass. In practical terms, there is a Lane Authority.
ai.rex: REX has the boarding party's sidearms at three. He has their patience at fewer than three. He recommends the inspection proceed briskly.
ai.chip: CHIP recommends full cooperation and a five-star rating! The inspector's ratings affect their bonus! Everybody's ratings affect somebody's bonus!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the inspector's 'biosecurity kit' is a cooler and a pair of shears. She leaves it to you what that means. She'd rather not, but she will.

revisit.body: The clamp is still on. The inspector is still holding the clipboard as if it were a warrant.

choices.sub: They want to see the growbay

inspect.title: THE INSPECTION
inspect.body: The inspector walks your growbay with a pair of shears and the air of a connoisseur. A cooler hums on a strap at their hip. They stop at the healthiest plant aboard, as people with shears always do.
inspect.line: This one's showing signs of something. We'll need a sample. A big sample.

ai.aria: They LIKE our crop! It's the best one they've seen! ARIA can tell by the shears!
ai.marv: MARV notes the 'sample' is about a fifth of the crop by mass. Contraband botany sells well at the outer stations. He has the prices. He wishes he didn't.
ai.rex: REX has positioned himself between the inspector and the crop, in the sense that he has turned the growbay lights up very bright.
ai.chip: CHIP notes that samples taken during inspection are non-refundable! Like most things! Like everything, really!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would point at the cooler and ask what else is in it, in front of their own crew. But you're the captain. Apparently.

choices.text: Ask what else is in the cooler

insp_talked.title: JURISDICTION
insp_talked.body: {crew.diplomat} asks to see the Lane Authority's charter, then its founding vote, then the minutes of the founding vote. The inspector takes one small, face-saving sample and unclamps before anyone asks to see the seal.
insp_talked.narrative: {crew.diplomat} argued jurisdiction with a self-appointed Lane Authority. They took a small sample and left.

insp_paid.title: FEE RECEIVED
insp_paid.body: The fee is accepted, the clipboard signed, the shears holstered. The cutter unclamps with a courteous bump. It is exactly like being robbed, except that you are thanked.
insp_paid.narrative: Paid a Lane Authority 'inspection fee' of twelve gold. Thanked for it, too.

insp_refused.title: FORCED
insp_refused.body: You refuse. They cut through the outer airlock seal anyway, take their sample at gunpoint, and leave a citation for 'obstruction' taped to the inner door. The seal will need work. The citation is framed by lunchtime.
insp_refused.narrative: Refused a Lane Authority boarding. They cut the airlock seal, took a sample anyway and left a citation.

insp_sample.title: SAMPLED
insp_sample.body: The inspector takes a fifth of the crop, labels it BIOHAZARD in a confident hand, and leaves. The cooler sounds heavier on the way out. The crew watched the whole thing and did nothing, and will be thinking about that for a while.
insp_sample.narrative: Let a Lane Authority inspector take a fifth of the crop as a 'sample.'

insp_cuttings.title: CUTTINGS
insp_cuttings.body: {crew.botanist} offers a tray of cuttings, prepared on the spot, with a short lecture on viability. The inspector, outmatched on botany, accepts the tray and the lecture. The crop loses a few stems. {crew.botanist} loses patience, briefly and audibly.
insp_cuttings.narrative: {crew.botanist} fobbed a Lane Authority inspector off with a tray of cuttings.

insp_cooler.title: CALLED
insp_cooler.body: You ask, in front of their crew, what else is in the cooler. The inspector's crew looks at the cooler. The inspector looks at the inspector's crew. The cutter unclamps so fast it takes a ring of your airlock seal with it, and is gone before anyone says 'contraband.'
insp_cooler.narrative: Asked a Lane Authority inspector what else was in the cooler. The cutter left in a hurry, with a ring of our airlock seal.

intro.title: THE WANTED LIST
intro.body: A small, immaculate ship drifts alongside, its running lights blinking in a courtesy pattern nobody has used in a century. Painted along its flank in careful serif capitals: THE MUSEUM OF THE BEFORE — ADMISSION BY BARTER. A list is already scrolling across your screen. It is headed WANTED. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Forgive the intrusion. Your ship is old enough to be interesting. Is anything in your hold older?

ai.aria: A museum! A flying museum! ARIA has always wanted to be in a museum! As a visitor! For now!
ai.marv: MARV has read the wanted list. It is mostly packaging. He has never seen anyone want packaging this much, and he has read a marketing department's mail.
ai.rex: REX scanned the ship. No weapons. Display cases, climate control and a frankly excessive dehumidifier. He is standing down.
ai.chip: CHIP is THRILLED! Branded heritage merchandise is a growth sector! CHIP's own logo will be collectible one day! CHIP has checked!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the curator keeps the list short on purpose. Whatever is on it, they pay above the odds for. Whatever isn't, they will politely not see, so please don't wave it at them.

wanted.title: WANTED
wanted.body: The list is short, specific and written with the tenderness most people save for letters. Analog recordings, still sealed. Anything bearing the logo of a company that no longer exists. Relics from before, in any condition the curator can describe as honest. At the bottom, in smaller type: duplicates for sale.
wanted.line: I don't haggle over the Before. I pay what a thing is worth to me, and it is worth a great deal to me.

ai.aria: We might have something on the list! ARIA is checking the hold! ARIA is checking it again, harder!
ai.marv: MARV has compared the curator's prices with a station trader's. The curator pays more for what is on the list. He notes that this is what a list is for.
ai.rex: REX does not understand why anyone wants a sealed record they will never open. He would like it known that this is not the same as not wanting one.
ai.chip: CHIP calls this a seller's market! Rare! Beautiful! CHIP is straightening a tie he doesn't have!
ai.ajoy: AJOY points out that the curator pays one flat price for any relic. A good piece is worth more than that and a poor one less. Without a spectrometer aboard, nobody here knows which yours is, the curator included. She's sure you'll guess well.

choices.sub: One flat price, whatever it is worth

choices.text: Buy a tin of pre-collapse peaches — 9 gold
Buy a medkit from the duplicates — 10 gold

tour.title: THE COLLECTION
tour.body: The airlock opens onto a corridor of glass cases, each lit from below and labeled by hand. A toaster. A plastic bag, flattened and framed. A child's shoe with a light in the heel that, the card explains, once came on when you walked. The curator walks you past each one as if introducing relatives.
tour.line: Everything here was thrown away by someone. That's what makes it precious. Nobody keeps what they think will last.

ai.aria: ARIA loves the shoe! ARIA wants to know where the other shoe is! The card says nobody knows! ARIA is devastated and delighted!
ai.marv: MARV has cataloged the cases. He estimates the collection weighs less than one of our water tanks and is worth more than the ship. He has stopped estimating.
ai.rex: REX has been standing in front of the plastic bag for some time. He says it is tactically interesting. It is not tactically interesting.
ai.chip: CHIP spotted the logos of brands CHIP's parent company bought and shut down! CHIP is having a feeling! CHIP doesn't know what it's called!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes an empty case near the end, lit and labeled PENDING. The curator glances at it every time they pass. She'd fill it, if you have the thing. You walked past it twice.

choices.text: Donate the memorabilia to the empty case
choices.sub: No gold, but it stays somewhere

coll_polite_pass.title: PLEASANTRIES EXCHANGED
coll_polite_pass.body: You swap route news. The curator asks, with real interest, what the inner systems are throwing away these days, and writes down every answer.
coll_polite_pass.narrative: Route news traded for a curator's curiosity. The crew enjoyed being asked about their own rubbish as if it mattered.

coll_ignored.title: HAIL DECLINED
coll_ignored.body: You let the hail lapse. The museum holds alongside a little longer, its wanted list still scrolling, then glides off in search of an older ship.
coll_ignored.narrative: You ignored the hail. The Museum of the Before moved on, one exhibit short of whatever it was hoping for.

coll_sold_vinyl.title: ACQUIRED
coll_sold_vinyl.body: The curator receives the record in white gloves and tilts it to the light at an angle that shows every crease in the shrinkwrap. There are none. They make a sound that is not quite a word. The gold arrives before they have finished making it.
coll_sold_vinyl.line: Sealed. Actually sealed. You have no idea what you've done for me.
coll_sold_vinyl.narrative: Sold the sealed record to a traveling museum, for more than any station would pay and rather less than the curator would have.

coll_sold_memorabilia.title: ACQUIRED
coll_sold_memorabilia.body: The curator turns the piece over, finds the logo, and reads the company's name aloud with the care of someone reading a headstone. It goes into a padded case marked FOR THE GALLERY.
coll_sold_memorabilia.narrative: Sold a piece of corporate memorabilia to a collector who knew more about the company than its own staff ever did.

coll_sold_artifact.title: ACQUIRED
coll_sold_artifact.body: The curator does not ask what the relic is worth. They ask where it was found, and how, and by whom, and write every answer on its card before the price comes up. The price is the one on the list. It does not move.
coll_sold_artifact.line: Whatever it's worth to anyone else, this is what it's worth to me.
coll_sold_artifact.narrative: Sold a pre-collapse relic at the curator's flat price. Whether that was a bargain depends on which relic it was, and nobody aboard can say.

coll_bought_peaches.title: FROM THE ARCHIVE
coll_bought_peaches.body: The tin is older than anyone aboard and has outlived the company that sealed it. Opened at dinner, it turns out to contain peaches, and the peaches turn out to be excellent. Nobody can explain this. Nobody tries.
coll_bought_peaches.narrative: Bought a tin of pre-collapse peaches. They were excellent, which is either a triumph of canning or a small miracle, and the crew has decided it is both.

coll_bought_medkit.title: FROM THE DUPLICATES
coll_bought_medkit.body: The medkit comes out of a cabinet labeled DUPLICATES — DO NOT DISPLAY. It is sealed, in date, and the only thing aboard the museum that is meant to be used.
coll_bought_medkit.narrative: Bought a spare medkit off a museum's duplicates shelf. The least interesting thing they own, and the most useful thing we bought all week.

coll_tour.title: THE FULL TOUR
coll_tour.body: The tour takes two days. Nobody minds. The crew comes back quieter than they left, talking about the shoe and the toaster and the bag, and about which of their own things might sit in a case like that one day.
coll_tour.narrative: Took the full tour of a traveling museum of thrown-away things. The crew came back thoughtful, which is rarer out here than fuel.

coll_donated.title: PENDING, NO LONGER
coll_donated.body: You give the memorabilia to the empty case. The curator writes a new card by hand while you watch, and the card has the ship's name on it, spelled correctly, which is more than most official documents manage.
coll_donated.line: It will be here long after both of us. That's the whole idea.
coll_donated.narrative: Gave a piece of corporate memorabilia to a traveling museum. The ship's name is on a card in a glass case now, and the crew keeps bringing it up.

intro.title: OPENING OFFER
intro.body: A broad, slow freighter heaves alongside with every hatch open and hung with goods, like washing on a line. Before you have finished reading the prices on your screen, the trader has raised them. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: Look at all the hatches! It's like a market and a ship had a baby! A very expensive baby!
ai.marv: MARV has read the price list. Every figure on it is well above what a station charges. He believes the trader knows this. He believes the trader is counting on us knowing it.
ai.rex: REX notes the trader has crew on every hatch and prices on every screen. He respects a defended position.
ai.chip: CHIP recognizes these prices! They're anchor prices! CHIP invented anchor prices! CHIP did not invent anchor prices, but CHIP has always admired them!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has read this trader's last few sales on the lane log. Every customer paid less than the list, and not one of them paid their first offer. She'd hate for you to be the exception.

prices.title: THE ASKING PRICE
prices.body: The manifest is honest about everything except value. Fuel cells, ration crates, hull patches, all priced as though the trader were the last ship in the galaxy and had just been told so. Under each price, in a smaller hand, is the word NEGOTIABLE.
prices.line: Those are the prices. They're not the price. Learn the difference and we'll get on fine.

ai.aria: NEGOTIABLE! ARIA's favorite word that isn't FREE!
ai.marv: MARV advises against paying list. He also advises against haggling badly, which costs more than list. He has modeled our haggling. He would like a diplomat.
ai.rex: REX recommends paying nothing. He concedes this is not a commercial strategy.
ai.chip: CHIP can authorize a counter-offer! CHIP can authorize anything! CHIP's authority is mostly emotional!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the prices fall fastest for someone who enjoys this. If nobody aboard enjoys it, pay the list or walk. Haggling while miserable is how they win. She has seen you haggle.

choices.text: Haggle for the fuel cell — 10 gold
choices.detail: Needs 20 gold on hand: a wobble costs extra.

choices.sub: Slow · and they will enjoy it

bargain.title: THE LONG CONVERSATION
bargain.body: Your diplomat opens with a compliment about the freighter's paintwork, moves on to a story about a cousin, and does not mention money for a very long time. The trader leans in. Two people who enjoy this are in the same conversation at last, and the prices on the screen begin, one by one, to fall.
bargain.line: Oh, you're good. You're very good. Fine. But only because I like you.

ai.aria: They're FRIENDS now! ARIA can see it! Commerce is a love language!
ai.marv: MARV has watched the prices fall to station rates and then below them. He notes that this is a two-day conversation, and that the days are part of the price.
ai.rex: REX has timed the conversation. He has stopped timing the conversation. Nothing is under threat except the schedule.
ai.chip: CHIP is taking notes! SO many notes! CHIP will be using these techniques on you later!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the trader is now giving away the margin and enjoying it. She recommends buying before they remember who they are.

hag_polite_pass.title: PLEASANTRIES EXCHANGED
hag_polite_pass.body: You swap route gossip. The trader tries to sell you the gossip back at a markup, laughs, and burns off towards a customer with less patience.
hag_polite_pass.narrative: Route gossip exchanged free of charge, which the trader took as a personal loss and the crew took as a small victory.

hag_ignored.title: HAIL DECLINED
hag_ignored.body: You let the hail lapse. The freighter holds alongside, lowering its prices on the screen one at a time, until it is out of range and still lowering them.
hag_ignored.narrative: You ignored the hail. The trader's last price, as they drifted out of range, was nearly reasonable.

hag_fuel_list.title: PAID IN FULL
hag_fuel_list.body: You pay the asking price. The trader accepts it with the pained look of someone who wanted the argument more than the gold, and sends the fuel cell across with a small sigh.
hag_fuel_list.narrative: Bought a fuel cell at the asking price. It works exactly as well as a cheap one. The crew has opinions about that.

hag_food_list.title: PAID IN FULL
hag_food_list.body: The ration crate crosses on a cargo line with the price still taped to it, as a souvenir.
hag_food_list.narrative: Bought a ration crate at the asking price. The rations are fine. The price tag is still on the crate, and nobody has the heart to take it off.

hag_fuel_haggled.title: A PRICE, EVENTUALLY
hag_fuel_haggled.body: You counter. They counter. You counter the counter. Somewhere in the back-and-forth a price gets agreed, and the fuel cell comes across on the cargo line with the receipt taped to it.
hag_fuel_haggled.line: See? That wasn't so hard. It was a little hard.
hag_fuel_haggled.narrative: Haggled for a fuel cell. Whether the price was fair depends on who is telling it.

hag_fuel_wobbled.title: TALKED UP
hag_fuel_wobbled.body: You counter, and your voice catches halfway through the number. The trader hears it. Every counter after that goes their way, and the cell comes across at the full asking price.
hag_fuel_wobbled.line: Nerves are extra. Everybody knows that.
hag_fuel_wobbled.narrative: Tried to haggle for a fuel cell and paid the full price for the attempt. The crew has stopped bringing it up, mostly.

hag_declined.title: NO SALE
hag_declined.body: You decline. The trader drops every price on the list at once, watches you decline again, and puts them all back up with the dignity of a person who has tried everything.
hag_declined.narrative: No sale. The prices fell, briefly, as we left. It was too late for both of us.

hag_fuel_bargain.title: A FRIEND'S PRICE
hag_fuel_bargain.body: The fuel cell comes across with a receipt that says FRIEND'S PRICE in the trader's own hand, underlined. The conversation that produced it took two days, and your diplomat would happily have gone on.
hag_fuel_bargain.narrative: Bought a fuel cell at a friend's price, after two days' conversation. The diplomat calls it the best two days of the trip.

hag_food_bargain.title: A FRIEND'S PRICE
hag_food_bargain.body: The ration crate arrives with FRIEND'S PRICE written on the lid and a jar of something pickled on top, which nobody asked for and nobody refuses. The conversation that produced it took two days.
hag_food_bargain.narrative: Bought a ration crate at a friend's price, after two days' conversation. The pickles were a gift. The pickles were good.

hag_patch_bargain.title: A FRIEND'S PRICE
hag_patch_bargain.body: The hull patch crosses with FRIEND'S PRICE on its wrapper and the trader's private comm code under that, in case you are ever back this way and want to talk for two days again.
hag_patch_bargain.narrative: Bought a hull patch at a friend's price, after two days' conversation, and came away with the trader's comm code as well.

intro.title: EVERYTHING MUST GO
intro.body: A gleaming ship pulls up much too fast and stops much too neatly, banners unrolling down its hull: CLOSING DOWN — EVERYTHING MUST GO — NO REASONABLE OFFER REFUSED. The paint is fresh. The banners are fresh. The ship's registry, when you look it up, is fresher than both. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Friends. Friends. You have caught me on the worst day of my life, which makes it the best day of yours.

ai.aria: A closing-down sale! Everything must go! ARIA wants to help everything go! Into our hold!
ai.marv: MARV has run the registry. The ship was registered this week. By its own banner, the sale has been closing down since before that. He is sharing this without comment.
ai.rex: REX does not like a merchant who smiles with that many teeth. He has no evidence. He is not a court. He is REX.
ai.chip: CHIP rates this offer AMAZING! CHIP is required to add that CHIP rates every offer amazing! CHIP has been asked to stop!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would look hardest at whatever they are most eager to sell, and she would look at it from the inside. You'll look at the price tag. She knows.

pitch.title: ONE DAY ONLY
pitch.body: The deals scroll past faster than you can read them, which may be the point. The headline item glows at the top of the screen: a crate of hull plating, factory sealed, at a price well under anything a station would ask. Lower down sits a produce crate described as farm fresh, from a farm the listing declines to name.

ai.aria: Hull plating! At that price! ARIA has never seen a better deal! ARIA has never seen this deal at all, which makes it rarer!
ai.marv: MARV notes that hull plating at this price is stolen, damaged, or not hull plating. He has ranked the options by how much he would like to be wrong.
ai.rex: REX would open the crate before paying for the crate. That is not advice. It is a lifestyle.
ai.chip: CHIP can offer an extended warranty on the plating! CHIP cannot offer an extended warranty on the plating! CHIP has just read the plating!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the produce is real. She does not say anything about anything else, which you may take as saying it.

choices.text: Let {crew.diplomat} ask where it came from

exposed.title: FACTORY SEALED
exposed.body: The seal on the crate lifts with a fingernail. Inside, nested in a great deal of packing foam carved lovingly into the shape of hull plating, is a single hull patch. The trader looks at the patch, then at you, then at the patch again, with the expression of someone genuinely, deeply surprised to be caught.
exposed.line: Well. That's — I've never seen that crate before in my life. Let's be friends about this.

ai.aria: It's a hull patch! That's nearly hull plating! It's hull plating's little cousin! ARIA still loves it!
ai.marv: MARV would like the record to show that he ranked this outcome first. He would also like it to show that he took no pleasure in it. He took some pleasure in it.
ai.rex: REX recommends telling everyone on the lane. Loudly. With the registry.
ai.chip: CHIP is shocked! CHIP is appalled! CHIP is, professionally speaking, a little impressed by the foam!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the trader will now do almost anything to keep this off the lane log. Almost anything is a lot. So is a lane log nobody else gets fooled by, but she's sure you'll weigh that carefully.

choices.text: Pay what the patch is worth — 8 gold
Take a fuel cell for your silence
choices.sub: Free, and the lane never hears

choices.text: Warn the lane on the open channel
choices.sub: The ship, the trick and the foam

con_polite_pass.title: PLEASANTRIES EXCHANGED
con_polite_pass.body: You exchange route news. The trader agrees with everything you say, warmly, including the parts that contradict each other, and burns off towards the next customer in a hurry.
con_polite_pass.narrative: Route news exchanged with a trader who agreed with all of it. The crew is still working out what that means.

con_ignored.title: HAIL DECLINED
con_ignored.body: You let the hail lapse. The banners stay up as the ship pulls away. The last one you can read says FINAL DAY. It looks well used.
con_ignored.narrative: You ignored the hail. The closing-down sale went on closing down somewhere else.

con_plating_blind.title: FACTORY SEALED
con_plating_blind.body: The crate comes aboard with a great deal of ceremony and a seal that peels off at a touch. Inside, nested in packing foam carved lovingly into the shape of hull plating, is one hull patch. By the time anyone thinks to call the trader back, the banners are a speck.
con_plating_blind.narrative: Paid hull-plating money for a hull patch in a very large box. The foam was beautiful. The crew has started calling the patch 'the plating'.

con_produce.title: FARM FRESH
con_produce.body: The produce crate is exactly what it claims to be, apart from the farm, the freshness and the word crate, which is generous for a box. The food is real. The crew eats it in a slightly suspicious silence.
con_produce.narrative: Bought a box of produce at a closing-down sale. It was real food, which turned out to be the only thing at that sale that was.

con_declined.title: NO SALE
con_declined.body: You decline. The trader lowers the price of the plating, then lowers it again, then offers to throw in the banners. You decline the banners too.
con_declined.narrative: No sale. The plating got cheaper as we left, which said everything about the plating.

con_patch_fair.title: PRICED HONESTLY
con_patch_fair.body: You pay a fair price for the patch, and only for the patch. The trader takes the gold with the stiff dignity of someone who has never been paid a fair price before and finds it faintly insulting.
con_patch_fair.narrative: Bought a hull patch for what it was worth from a trader who had been selling it as plating. Fair, in the end, though nobody involved had planned on fair.

con_hush.title: OFF THE RECORD
con_hush.body: A fuel cell crosses on a cargo line, with no receipt. The lane log will hear nothing. The crew watches the closing-down sale pull away towards its next customer, and nobody says anything for a while.
con_hush.narrative: Took a fuel cell to keep quiet about a con. The cell works fine. The silence weighs more than it does.

con_warned.title: PUBLIC SERVICE
con_warned.body: You put it all on the open channel: the ship, the registry, the crate, the foam. Within minutes other ships on the lane answer with their own stories about the same banners. The trader is gone before the last of them has finished.
con_warned.line: You'll regret — no. No, you won't, will you. Fine.
con_warned.narrative: Warned the lane about a closing-down sale that never closed. Other ships answered with their own stories, and the crew felt, for once, like part of something.

intro.title: LEARNER'S PERMIT
intro.body: A pirate ship drops in off your bow with every gun run out and a white square on its nose, a red L painted in the middle of it. Behind the captain's chair on the screen sits someone older with a clipboard and the stillness of a person who has done this many times and is now marking somebody else doing it. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: Hail, little ship. Cut your engines. We'll make this — sorry. We WILL make this quick. Sorry.

ai.aria: A student! They're learning! ARIA believes in them! ARIA believes in everyone, but ARIA especially believes in this one!
ai.marv: MARV notes the guns are real and the trainee's hands are not steady. He considers this the most dangerous combination available.
ai.rex: REX reads one live crew and one assessor. The assessor is the threat. The kid is the risk.
ai.chip: CHIP sees a career-development moment! CHIP offers mentorship packages! CHIP's mentorship packages are mostly invoices!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says the examiner wants a clean pass, not a payday, and the kid wants to go home. You can give them either. The pass costs less than the tribute, if the diplomat does the talking. She'd have thought that was obvious.

revisit.body: The red L is still on their nose. The examiner has turned a page.

choices.sub: They take a share of the tank, slowly
Burn fuel, leave the lesson behind

coach.title: THE PRACTICAL
coach.body: Your diplomat opens a second channel, to the examiner, and asks politely how the assessment is weighted. The examiner, who has not been asked a question by a target in years, answers in full. The trainee listens to all of it with the face of someone learning that their exam has a back door.
coach.line: Marks for control. Marks for restraint. Marks off for shooting anyone you didn't need to. They always forget the restraint.

ai.aria: We're helping them STUDY! ARIA loves studying! ARIA has never studied! ARIA was born knowing things, some of them true!
ai.marv: MARV observes that restraint is worth marks, and that our gold is worth less to them than a pass. He recommends selling them the pass.
ai.rex: REX does not coach the opposition. He notes, for the record, that the kid's stance is wrong and getting worse.
ai.chip: CHIP is drafting a study guide! A premium study guide! With practice robberies! Of other ships! Not ours!
ai.ajoy: AJOY would point out the step they skipped: they never checked our transponder. Say so and the examiner fails them on procedure, and it costs us no gold. Someone will be disappointed, and it won't be you.

choices.sub: A token tribute · a cleaner pass
The examiner fails them on procedure

lp_paid.title: A CLEAN PASS
lp_paid.body: The tribute transfers. The trainee says thank you, remembers they are not supposed to, and says it again anyway. The examiner makes a mark. The red L stays pointed at you until you are out of sight.
lp_paid.narrative: Paid a learner pirate's tribute in full. Somewhere behind us a student passed an exam, and our gold paid for it.

lp_siphon.title: THE PRACTICAL ELEMENT
lp_siphon.body: The trainee mates a hose to your fuel port after several attempts and siphons with enormous care while the examiner narrates everything they are doing wrong. They take their share of the tank, label it, and thank you for your patience.
lp_siphon.narrative: Let a trainee pirate practice siphoning on our fuel tank. They took their share with great care, and got a good mark for it.

lp_flee.title: LESSON INTERRUPTED
lp_flee.body: You pour fuel into the engines and go. The trainee gives chase strictly by the book, which is slowly, while the examiner writes something that takes a long time to write.
lp_flee.narrative: Ran from a learner pirate. They chased by the book. The book is not fast.

lp_token.title: SHOWS RESTRAINT
lp_token.body: The trainee asks for a token tribute, takes it, and wishes you a safe journey in a voice that almost doesn't shake. The examiner makes a long mark and, for the first time, smiles. Your diplomat is unbearable about it for a day.
lp_token.line: Thank you. I mean — move along. Thank you.
lp_token.narrative: Coached a learner pirate to a pass for a token tribute. The examiner smiled. The crew is oddly proud.

lp_procedure.title: FAIL
lp_procedure.body: The examiner looks at the trainee. The trainee looks at the examiner. A long, quiet moment passes in which a career is reconsidered. The guns retract, and the channel stays open just long enough for you to hear the debrief begin.
lp_procedure.line: Transponder. Every time. We'll go again next week.
lp_procedure.narrative: Pointed out a trainee pirate's missed step. They failed and turned for home. Free passage, and a quiet crew afterwards.

lp_bluff.title: CALLED
lp_bluff.body: The examiner asks for your examiner's number. You do not have an examiner's number. Nobody on your bridge has heard of an examiner's number. The trainee is told, quietly, that this is now the practical.

intro.title: HUNGRY COMPANY
intro.body: The ship that cuts across your course was a family hauler once, and still is: there are drawings taped to the inside of its viewport and a row of small helmets clipped beside the airlock. The person on the screen holds a mining laser the way you hold something you have only read about. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: We don't want your gold. Gold doesn't feed anybody out here. Food. Whatever you've got that a child will eat.

ai.aria: They have KIDS! The drawings are lovely! One of them is a horse! Or a ship! A horse-ship! ARIA loves it!
ai.marv: MARV has scanned the hauler. Its stores are nearly empty and its drive is in worse shape than their aim. He does not think they can follow us. He does not think they can go anywhere.
ai.rex: REX reads one weapon, one operator, untrained. Threat low. He would like that taken as an assessment and not a suggestion.
ai.chip: CHIP's systems don't have a category for this! CHIP is filing it under customer service! CHIP isn't sure that's right!
ai.ajoy: AJOY says whatever you choose, they will remember this ship. She'd prefer it remembered for something other than your first instinct.

revisit.body: The drawings are still taped to their viewport. The laser has not moved, and neither has the hand holding it.

talk.title: AROUND THE TABLE
talk.body: Your diplomat asks their names, then their children's names, then where they were headed before the drive gave out. The laser drifts lower while they answer. Somewhere off screen a small voice asks whether the other ship has biscuits.
talk.line: We were going to the colony. Same as you, probably. We just set off with less.

ai.aria: We're friends now! ARIA can tell! ARIA can always tell! ARIA is right this time!
ai.marv: MARV has read the hauler's fault codes. Most of them are one fault. He believes an engineer could clear it in a few days. He is not volunteering anyone. He is noting.
ai.rex: REX has lowered the threat assessment to nothing. He would like it known that this was always the likely outcome and that he was ready anyway.
ai.chip: CHIP has located a relief office at the next station! CHIP has also located its fees! CHIP is choosing not to mention its fees!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes that a shared meal goes further than a ration crate, and a working drive goes furthest of all. She's only mentioning the drive because nobody else has.

choices.text: "Eat with us. Both crews, one table."
"There's a relief office at the next station."

hf_rations.title: FED
hf_rations.body: You send a ration crate across on a cargo line. The laser goes down before the crate has finished crossing. Through the viewport, between the drawings, small hands have the lid off before the adults can get to it.
hf_rations.line: Thank you. We won't — thank you.
hf_rations.narrative: Gave rations to a family crew who held us up with a mining laser. Nobody aboard regrets it.

hf_gold.title: PAID
hf_gold.body: You offer gold. They take it, because there is nothing else on offer, and the look they give it says exactly what it is worth out here. The hauler limps off towards the nearest station, which is not near.
hf_gold.line: It'll buy food. Somewhere. Thank you, I suppose.
hf_gold.narrative: Paid a hungry family crew in gold instead of food. They took it. It may get them as far as a market.

hf_fire.title: NOTHING LEFT TO LOSE
hf_fire.body: Your guns come up. On their screen, someone takes the drawings down off the viewport, one at a time, before they answer.
hf_fire.line: Then we've got nothing to lose, have we.

hf_flee.title: LEFT BEHIND
hf_flee.body: You burn away. They try to follow, and their drive coughs, steadies, and coughs again. You watch the hauler on the rear sensors until it is too small to watch, and then for a while after that.
hf_flee.narrative: Outran a family crew whose drive could barely hold them. It was not hard. Nobody aboard is talking about how easy it was.

hf_dinner.title: ONE TABLE
hf_dinner.body: {crew.chef} takes what would have fed one crew and makes it feed two, by a method involving a great deal of broth and no explanations. The children eat first. The adults eat second. Everyone eats more than they expected to.
hf_dinner.line: Best meal we've had since we left. Since before we left.
hf_dinner.narrative: {crew.chef} cooked one meal for two crews. It stretched. The family left fed, and the crew left better than fed.

hf_drive.title: UNDER THE HOOD
hf_drive.body: {crew.engineer} spends days in the hauler's engine bay, finds the fault buried under somebody's last repair, and clears it. The drive comes up clean. By the time it does, the children have drawn {crew.engineer} a picture. It goes on the wall above the workbench.
hf_drive.line: It runs. It actually runs. We'll tell everyone about you.
hf_drive.narrative: {crew.engineer} fixed a stranded family's drive. It cost days. The drawing they sent back is on the workshop wall now.

hf_directions.title: DIRECTIONS
hf_directions.body: Your diplomat gives them the station, the office, the name of the one person at the office worth asking for, and a bag of something to keep the children going until then. They write it all down and read it back.
hf_directions.line: The name, again? Thank you. Thank you.
hf_directions.narrative: Pointed a hungry family towards a relief office, with a little food to get them there.
